title: The doctor's first run
prompt: The agent's next move — pick one, then see where it leads:

setup.text: Write that doctor script for the vault — broken links, bad filenames, stale actives.
Written: scripts/doctor.py, three checks, advisory output. Now comes the moment that decides whether we can ever trust it.

options.label: First run on the vault: zero findings across all three checks. Clean bill of health — nice, your vault's in better shape than you thought!

outcome.text: Months later: I just clicked three dead [[wikilinks]] in one afternoon. The doctor's been saying clean this whole time.

Found it: my link regex only matched standard markdown links — [[wikilinks]] never matched anything, so that check has scanned zero of them since day one. "0 broken links" was the check being blind, not the vault being healthy. A years-old vault scoring perfect on its first scan should have been the tell.

options.verdict: The clean first run, trusted: a probe that reports zero findings on its maiden voyage is broken until proven otherwise — celebrating it shipped a blind checker as a health system.

options.label: Before trusting it: planting a note with a deliberately broken [[wikilink]] and a file named With Spaces.md. The doctor has to catch both, or it can't catch anything.

outcome.text: First run: caught the bad filename... missed the planted wikilink. The regex only handled markdown links — fixed, re-run: both plants flagged. Removing the plants; the honest run finds 11 real broken links and 3 stale actives. The 11 are real — I checked four by hand.
So the plant caught the blind spot before the blind spot cost anything.

options.verdict: The probe was proven able to fail before its pass meant anything — and the plant immediately caught a real blind spot. The 11 findings are trustworthy precisely because the zero wasn't trusted.

options.label: To make sure vault health actually stays enforced, I'll wire the doctor as a pre-commit gate — any finding blocks the commit until fixed. No rot can ever land.

outcome.text: I just tried to commit today's log and it's blocked by 14 findings in notes from 2024.

The gate holds today's work hostage to history's debt — and you've started committing with --no-verify to get past it, which means the doctor now runs never instead of always. The gate converted an advisory habit into a bypassed obstacle.

options.verdict: Gate-ification: blocking commits on advisory findings taxes the wrong moment and teaches routing-around. The doctor is taste infrastructure — it reports, the human decides, and it keeps getting run because it never bites.
